picks.title: Saudi National Arrested for Installing Surreptitious Audio Recording Device at OpenAI
picks.excerpt: DOJ says an OpenAI employee, a Saudi national, was arrested and charged with using or trying to use a device to intercept oral communications after a recording device was found hidden in an OpenAI conference room in San Francisco.
picks.rationale: Primary document: a new federal arrest and charge over a hidden recording device at a frontier AI lab, which bears on AI-lab security and foreign access. Describe the person only as charged, and do not suggest a state link beyond what DOJ says. The Verge report on the same arrest is the same story and is not used.

picks.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Tell British Lawmakers: Regulate Us
picks.excerpt: AI company leaders joined whistleblowers and security officials at a broad UK parliamentary session and asked lawmakers for regulation. Nearby, Britain's spy chief warned that AI could be used to create new bioweapons.
picks.rationale: New event: frontier labs testified to the UK Parliament and asked for regulation. Attribute each position to the named company. Keep the copy on the regulation testimony and leave out the bioweapon aside entirely, because of the biosecurity classifier risk.

picks.title: The Biggest Pro-AI Super PAC Network Has Poured Millions Into Nevada Shell Companies
picks.excerpt: Leading the Future, a super PAC network backed by Silicon Valley figures, has raised large sums to support pro-AI candidates in both parties and has routed millions through Nevada shell companies, WIRED reports.
picks.rationale: Elections axis: AI-industry money in the midterms, based on new campaign-finance findings. AI is central because the PAC exists to back AI policy. Stay non-partisan: it is bipartisan spending, attribute the findings to WIRED's reporting and the filings, and add no horse-race framing.

picks.title: The Many Open Questions About the Trump Administration's New De Facto AI Model Licensing System
picks.excerpt: Adam Conner (Center for American Progress) argues the confidential AI framework created under the June 2026 executive order works as a de facto licensing system for frontier models, with no public answer on which models are covered or who gets early access. He notes the government has agreed to release the framework text by Oct. 30.
picks.rationale: Directly relevant to builders: a confidential frontier-model framework that gates access, and the government has committed to publish its text by Oct. 30. Lead with the facts (the EO, the confidential framework, the Oct. 30 release commitment), and present 'de facto licensing' as the author's argument, attributed to Conner and CAP.

picks.title: Home Office asylum AI flunks one in five accuracy checks
picks.excerpt: Ministers promised the UK Home Office's AI tools would speed up asylum decisions. Campaigners say the technology fails one in five accuracy checks, and processing times are getting longer.
picks.rationale: Government AI deployment under accountability scrutiny, with concrete accuracy figures. Attribute the failure-rate claim to the campaigners and their data source, and include the Home Office response if the article has one.

alternates.title: (LEAD) Arms agency to accelerate development of nuclear-powered subs, AI-driven combat systems
alternates.excerpt: South Korea's Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA) told lawmakers it will speed up development of nuclear-powered submarines and AI-driven combat systems.
alternates.rationale: Backup geopolitics pick. It is a new agency policy statement, separate from the 10-13 Pangyo AX hub card, but the AI element shares the headline with nuclear subs. Dedup: follow-up, nearest https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261012006500315, new_action: DAPA procurement-acceleration plan reported to the National Assembly.
